summary: Redwood team walked Sterling through what admin and audit logs capture, export options, retention defaults and enterprise customization, and alignment with SOC2/ISO controls. Customer primarily focused on admin activity (user/role/API-key changes), immutable storage and long-term retention for audits.
There was an ask for a sample log export and to validate ingestion into Sterling's SIEM (Splunk). Next step is test export and share compliance artifacts.
topics: What audit events are captured (admin activity vs request logs)
Retention defaults and long-term retention options
transcript: 00:00:01 - Evan Kim: Hey everyone thanks for joining, Evan from Redwood inference on the line, with Priya our solutions engineer and Liam from CSM. how's everyone doing?
00:00:10 - Marco Alvarez: Hi Evan, thanks. we have about 45 minutes, want to use it to understand exactly what you capture in audit logs and how we can retain/export them for our audits.

00:00:23 - Priya Shah: Great, Marco. quick agenda: we'll run through admin activity events, request-level logs, export paths, retention policies, and controls like immutability and KMS. then leave time for questions and next steps.

00:00:38 - Samantha Price: A couple specific asks up front — for compliance we need immutable admin logs for at least 3 years, and also want to validate ingestion into Splunk. Also we use AWS KMS for keys and want to ensure you support customer-managed keys.

00:00:55 - Priya Shah: Absolutely. high level — Redwood separates two families of logs: 1) admin & control plane events (user creation, role changes, SSO/SAML events, SCIM provisioning, API key creation/revocation, RBAC changes, admin console activity), and 2) request-level telemetry (request id, model used, response latencies, token counts). For this call we'll focus on the admin / audit trails you mentioned.
00:01:22 - Daniel Cho: when you say "request-level" does that include prompts? we need to ensure PII is not leaking into long-term storage — some of our teams log prompts currently.

00:01:32 - Priya Shah: Good question. by default, prompt/response payloads are not included in admin audit logs. request logs can include metadata (request id, model version, latency, error codes) but payload capture is configurable and off by default for hosted tiers. there is an option in Dedicated/Private where you can enable payload logging for troubleshooting, but we recommend anonymization and masking — and it's stored separately with tighter access controls and optional short retention windows.
00:02:05 - Marco Alvarez: ok that helps. can you explain export options? we want daily pushes into our Splunk instance and long-term archival in our S3 retention buckets.

00:02:18 - Priya Shah: Sure — we support multiple export mechanisms in parallel: a) scheduled JSON/NDJSON exported to customer S3 (we can push to your bucket with an assumed IAM role), b) streaming via HTTPS/webhook to a SIEM endpoint, c) cloud-native streams — CloudWatch/CloudTrail integration for AWS-hosted customers, and d) direct Splunk HEC or syslog forwarding. For Splunk specifically we can push HEC events or provide an S3 bucket for your ingestion jobs. The sample export contains structured fields: timestamp, actor, action, resource, org_id, request_id, ip_address, outcome, change_before, change_after (where applicable).
00:03:05 - Samantha Price: change_before/change_after is critical for us. does change_before include sensitive fields like full API key values?

00:03:13 - Priya Shah: No — we never store plaintext secrets in change_before or change_after. for API key rotation/creation events we capture metadata (key id, owner, expiry, scopes) and mark the secret value as redacted. We also log whether a key was exported, rotated or revoked.
00:03:35 - Marco Alvarez: what about immutability / append-only storage? auditors ask for tamper-evidence.

00:03:42 - Priya Shah: Logs are written to append-only storage in the control plane. For hosted customers, we provide an immutable export option: when enabled, exported files are signed (SHA256) and each file has a checksum plus a signing token. For enterprise Dedicated/Private deployments we can enable write-once-read-many (WORM) buckets on the customer side or help configure S3 Object Lock to meet retention and immutability requirements. We also support periodic signed manifests to prove chain-of-custody.
00:04:10 - Daniel Cho: How long do you keep admin logs by default? and can we increase it to 7 years?

00:04:17 - Priya Shah: Default retention for audit/admin logs is 90 days on the hosted plan. For enterprise plans we support customizable retention: 1 year, 3 years, or 7 years — retention longer than 1 year is a paid add-on and we can provide pricing. For Dedicated and Private, retention is fully configurable and you can write logs to your own archive for indefinite storage.
00:04:44 - Marco Alvarez: And encryption at rest and key management — do you support our AWS KMS CMK?

00:04:51 - Priya Shah: Yes. For hosted we support Redwood-managed keys by default, and we offer BYOK (bring-your-own-key) via AWS KMS or customer HSM for enterprise customers. With BYOK you control key rotation and access through your KMS policies. For Private installs you can configure HSM-backed keys and local KMS integrations. Access to the logs is restricted by RBAC; only users with the audit role or SRE roles can request exports and we log every export action as an auditable event.
00:05:20 - Samantha Price: Great. Does Redwood provide SAML/SSO events in the audit trail — like when someone fails to authenticate or when SCIM provisioning makes a change?

00:05:29 - Priya Shah: Yes — authentication events are captured: successful/failed logins, MFA events, SAML assertion failures, SCIM provisioning events with before/after for groups/users. Those events include ip_address, user_agent, and any available assertion id. We also surface suspicious login alerts and can forward them to your security webhook.
00:05:52 - Marco Alvarez: Are there rate limits on the export API? we plan heavy export during audits.

00:05:58 - Priya Shah: There are default rate limits to protect the control plane, but for enterprise customers we provision a dedicated export pipeline or provide a bulk export job for audits. We can run an on-demand bulk job to generate a complete export for a date range and drop it into your S3 bucket.

00:06:20 - Evan Kim: quick note — we'll attach a sample anonymized export to the follow-up email so you can validate field mapping into Splunk. Priya will run that export after we get the S3 details from Daniel.
00:06:31 - Daniel Cho: Ok I'll send the bucket name and an IAM role ARN after the call.
00:06:37 - Olivia Park: Any compliance attestations you can share? our auditors want SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence.

00:06:43 - Evan Kim: Yes we have both — we'll share the SOC 2 Type II report, ISO certificate, and our audit logs design doc. We'll also include a short note on how audit controls map to SOC 2 criteria.
00:06:56 - Marco Alvarez: On chain of custody — can you sign the export manifest with a Redwood key so we can present it to auditors?

00:07:03 - Priya Shah: We provide a signed manifest (HMAC/SHA256) for hosted exports. For Dedicated/Private we can coordinate a mutually agreed signing process, or you can configure S3 Object Lock and your own KMS to cryptographically sign objects.
00:07:20 - Samantha Price: A question on accessibility: who in our org can request exports? Our policy requires separation of duties — ops can request but compliance must approve first.

00:07:29 - Priya Shah: That's controlled by RBAC. We have granular roles: audit_reader, audit_admin, infra_admin, etc. Exports require audit_admin or a cross-team approval flow which we can wire into your SSO via SCIM groups. Each export request is itself logged with the requesting user, approver, and timestamps.
00:07:51 - Marco Alvarez: any support for SIEM enrichment — e.g., mapping Redwood actor IDs to our internal directory IDs?

00:07:58 - Priya Shah: We can include directory mappings in the export if you provide the mapping table, or include external_id fields (like your SAML NameID or SCIM externalId). We also support adding custom fields in the export manifest for easier correlation in Splunk.
00:08:18 - Daniel Cho: How do you handle log deletion requests? sometimes we have GDPR or Data Subject Access Request concerns.

00:08:25 - Priya Shah: Audit/admin logs are treated as system logs and are generally exempt from deletion for compliance reasons, but we do support data subject access controls for request logs where payloads were captured. For deletions we have a documented process and legal workflow. We can also mask or redact data on export if required.
00:08:46 - Marco Alvarez: Any known gaps we should be aware of?

00:08:49 - Priya Shah: Two things to note: 1) On hosted tier default retention is 90 days — if you need multi-year retention that's an enterprise add-on. 2) Prompt/response payloads are off by default and require explicit enable and controls; if teams enable payload capture we recommend scoping and masking to avoid long-term storage of PII. We'll call these out in the follow-up docs.
00:09:10 - Evan Kim: We'll also include a short checklist for auditors that maps Redwood controls to SOC 2 criterias — it'll speed your review.
00:09:18 - Samantha Price: Sounds good. one more operational Q — can exports be encrypted in transit to our S3? we need SSE-KMS on S3 and TLS in transit.

00:09:27 - Priya Shah: Yes — exports to S3 use TLS in transit; you can request SSE-KMS. When pushing to your bucket we honor your SSE-KMS settings and you can specify the CMK to use. For streaming endpoints we use TLS and can include mTLS for additional assurance.
00:09:47 - Marco Alvarez: Good. anything about monitoring/alerts? we'd like alerting when someone elevates privileges or when export jobs are requested.

00:09:55 - Priya Shah: We have built-in alerting hooks — you can configure alerts for specific admin events (role grant, API key creation, export requested) and forward them to Slack, PagerDuty, or a webhook. Alerts are configurable per-org and per-team.
00:10:10 - Daniel Cho: Ok timeline: we'll want to run a test export and validate Splunk ingestion within the next week if possible.
00:10:18 - Evan Kim: Noted. Priya will run the sample export once we have the bucket/role; Evan will send security pack and SOC docs. Liam will follow up to schedule the Splunk ingest test.
00:10:28 - Olivia Park: Thanks — also please include an item about how you handle forensic requests — sometimes auditors ask for raw event chains and timeline reconstruction.
00:10:36 - Priya Shah: We can provide a forensic export (full event chain for a given time window) as part of the enterprise package; it's a bulk job with chain-of-custody manifests and file signing.
00:10:50 - Marco Alvarez: ok that's it from our side. let's recap next steps.

00:10:55 - Evan Kim: Recap: 1) Evan send SOC2/ISO + controls mapping; 2) Priya create anonymized admin audit export and push to Sterling S3 for Splunk validation; 3) Daniel provide bucket and IAM role; 4) Liam schedule Splunk ingest test; 5) Olivia confirm retention requirement doc. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the ingest test. Anything else?
00:11:18 - Samantha Price: Nope that's all, thanks everyone.
00:11:22 - Marco Alvarez: Thanks, bye.
00:11:25 - (call ends)
00:11:30 - Notes: Actual audio had some brief crosstalk and there were minor transcription errors on product names (e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" transcribed as "Redwood dedicated" in a few places).
